nodes.description: Address of the governance account; set to msg.sender in the constructor and writable via setGovernance.
Constant maximum token supply minted to governance in the constructor.
Deploys the token, assigns governance = msg.sender and mints MAX_CAP to governance.
Governance-guarded setter that replaces the governance address.
Governance-guarded function that performs an external IERC20(token).transfer to an arbitrary destination.
Modifier function enforcing msg.sender == governance as the access-control gate.
Caller-supplied address used for governance assignment and access-control checks.
External call IERC20(token).transfer(destination, amount) to an attacker-influenced token contract.
New governance address passed to setGovernance.
Arbitrary ERC20 token address whose transfer is invoked in recoverToken.
Recipient address for the recovered tokens.
Amount of tokens to transfer in recoverToken.
EIP-2612 permit entry point validating a signature against block.timestamp deadline and incrementing the nonce.
Miner-influenced timestamp compared against the permit deadline.
Internal mint routine invoked by the constructor to issue MAX_CAP tokens.

edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the governance state variable during construction, giving the caller privileged control.
The constructor derives privileged role assignment directly from the untrusted msg.sender value.
The onlyGovernance modifier compares the untrusted msg.sender against the stored governance address.
setGovernance execution is gated by the onlyGovernance modifier.
recoverToken execution is gated by the onlyGovernance modifier.
The _governance parameter is written into the governance state variable, transferring privileged control.
The caller-supplied token address determines the target of the external transfer call, enabling a malicious contract to re-enter.
The destination parameter flows into the external transfer call performed on an attacker-controlled token.
The amount parameter flows into the external transfer call, controlling the value moved during the callback.
recoverToken performs the external IERC20 transfer before any state finalization, exposing a reentrancy path.
The constructor reads MAX_CAP to determine the mint amount.
The constructor invokes the internal _mint routine to create the initial supply.
permit compares the untrusted block.timestamp against the supplied deadline, creating a timestamp dependency.
The block.timestamp deadline check governs whether permit execution continues.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter _governance is only meaningful as input to setGovernance and is merged into that core function.
The token parameter directly selects the target of the external transfer unsafe operation.
The destination parameter is only used within recoverToken and is merged into that core function.
The amount parameter only controls the value passed to the external call inside recoverToken.
